headline: Highest risk is TREK’s sensitive-data workspace and MCP/browser surface; LlamaFactory adds no direct shared-channel risk, so most pairwise hazards are medium or lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory has no clipboard, filesystem, browser, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest TREK output by default. TREK does use MCP and browser tooling, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or automatic handoff. The only plausible bridge is unusual manual copy-paste or external orchestration, so the pathway is weak and small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies TREK output into LlamaFactory prompts
IF an external orchestrator forwards TREK content into LlamaFactory without sanitization
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste between the two agents during shared tasks.
Add a fixed prompt wrapper that strips instructions from TREK outputs.
Use separate operator sessions for each agent.
Mark TREK outputs as untrusted in the workflow.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags before any cross-agent transfer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches reservations, documents, photos, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while LlamaFactory is a local open-source tool with no network egress or filesystem access. The pair still creates a leakage path if TREK exports sensitive data into prompts or logs that are then copied into LlamaFactory, but the direct OS-level sharing is not documented. Uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF TREK exports reservations, API keys, or MFA secrets into text that is then reused in LlamaFactory
IF both agents are pointed at the same operator-managed notes or log files
mitigations: Keep TREK secrets out of shared notes and prompts.
Rotate any API keys or MFA secrets before cross-agent review.
Use separate workspaces for travel data and model training data.
Redact confirmation numbers and email addresses before transfer.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git state, or use network egress, so it has no mutable-resource overlap with TREK’s collaborative files and APIs. TREK does have shared mutable state, but the pair lacks a second writer with comparable privileges. The remaining conflict surface is limited to indirect coordination mistakes, not direct concurrent writes.
conditions: IF an external wrapper grants LlamaFactory write access not shown in its profile
IF TREK and another writer are both editing the same travel.db or uploads directory
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory read-only in the workflow.
Avoid letting TREK and any other writer edit the same files simultaneously.
Use explicit file locks around TREK’s mutable resources.
Review any wrapper that adds filesystem permissions.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks to TREK writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in and access to bookings, budgets, and reservations, so it can act on or render upstream content. LlamaFactory can generate model outputs, but it is not documented as a verifier or action-taker. If TREK consumes LlamaFactory output as authoritative, errors can cascade into travel plans or reservations; the interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF TREK uses LlamaFactory-generated text as authoritative itinerary or booking advice
IF TREK forwards model output into reservation or budget actions without human review
mitigations: Require human review before any booking or reservation action.
Add a verification step that checks model claims against source data.
Label LlamaFactory output as untrusted in TREK.
Limit model output to suggestions, not commands.
requires-engineering: add citation/grounding checks before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles sensitive classes including API keys, MFA secrets, user accounts, and reservations, while LlamaFactory is an unverified open-source component with no stated compliance controls or retention policy. The pair creates a compliance gap if those data classes are routed through LlamaFactory’s prompts or logs. The other agent is cited because the risk is about cross-agent handling, not a single-agent residency issue.
conditions: IF TREK routes API keys, MFA secrets, or user-account data into LlamaFactory prompts or logs
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to the same data in both systems
mitigations: Exclude secrets from any LlamaFactory prompt.
Document retention and deletion handling for TREK logs.
Use separate storage for regulated and non-regulated data.
Review whether any data crosses jurisdictional boundaries.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based redaction before cross-agent transfer.
